# amRml: machine learning for antimicrobial resistance prediction

<!-- badges: start -->
[![Lifecycle: experimental](https://img.shields.io/badge/lifecycle-experimental-orange.svg)](https://lifecycle.r-lib.org/articles/stages.html#experimental)
[![CRAN status](https://www.r-pkg.org/badges/version/amRml)](https://CRAN.R-project.org/package=amRml)
<!-- badges: end -->

amRml is part of the [amR suite](https://github.com/JRaviLab/amR) for antimicrobial resistance prediction. This package trains interpretable machine learning models using multi-scale genomic features from bacterial isolates.

## Overview

amRml provides functions to:

- Prepare ML-ready datasets from feature matrices
- Train interpretable logistic regression models
- Generate ranked feature importance lists
- Calculate comprehensive performance metrics
- Support parallel processing across drugs and species
- Export results for visualization in amRshiny

## Installation

### Current (development version)

```r
# Install from GitHub
if (!requireNamespace("remotes", quietly = TRUE))
    install.packages("remotes")

remotes::install_github("JRaviLab/amR_ml")
```

### Future (Bioconductor release)

Once submitted to Bioconductor, installation will be:

```r
if (!requireNamespace("BiocManager", quietly = TRUE))
    install.packages("BiocManager")

BiocManager::install("amRml")
```

## Quick start

```r
library(amRml)

# Load feature data from amRdata
features <- readRDS("features.rds")

# Train models for a single drug
models <- train_amr_models(
  features = features,
  drug = "ciprofloxacin",
  scales = c("gene", "protein", "domain", "struct"),
  model_type = "logistic_regression"
)

# View performance metrics
models$performance

# Extract top features
top_features <- get_top_features(models, n = 20)

# Train models across multiple drugs (parallel)
all_models <- train_multiple_drugs(
  features = features,
  drugs = c("ciprofloxacin", "tetracycline", "gentamicin"),
  parallel = TRUE,
  n_cores = 4
)
```

## Features

### Data preparation

The package processes feature matrices from amRdata to create ML-ready datasets:

- Subset isolates with available AST data for target drug
- Split samples into training and testing sets (stratified)
- Handle class imbalance through balanced sampling or weighting
- Normalize features when appropriate
- Filter low-variance features

### Model training

Uses the tidymodels framework for consistent, reproducible modeling:

- **Logistic regression**: Primary algorithm for interpretability
- Separate models per molecular scale (gene, protein, domain, struct)
- Combined multi-scale models using all features
- Cross-validation for hyperparameter tuning
- Support for custom model specifications

### Feature importance

Extracts ranked feature importance to identify resistance determinants:

- Coefficient magnitudes for logistic regression
- Permutation importance for other models (future)
- Scale-specific rankings
- Cross-drug comparison of features
- Integration with visualization tools

### Performance metrics

Comprehensive evaluation of model predictions:

- **Balanced accuracy**: Accounts for class imbalance
- **F1 score**: Harmonic mean of precision and recall
- **Matthews correlation coefficient (MCC)**: Overall classification quality
- **Sensitivity and specificity**: Per-class performance
- **Confusion matrices**: Detailed classification breakdown
- **ROC curves**: Threshold-independent evaluation

### Parallel processing

Efficient training across multiple models:

- Drug-level parallelization
- Scale-level parallelization
- Progress tracking for long-running jobs
- Automatic resource management

## Workflow example

Complete ML workflow for *Campylobacter jejuni*:

```r
library(amRml)

# Load features from amRdata
features <- arrow::read_parquet("cjej_features.parquet")
metadata <- arrow::read_parquet("cjej_metadata.parquet")

# Prepare ML datasets
ml_data <- prepare_ml_data(
  features = features,
  metadata = metadata,
  drug = "ciprofloxacin",
  test_fraction = 0.2,
  balance_classes = TRUE
)

# Train models across all scales
models <- train_amr_models(
  ml_data = ml_data,
  scales = c("gene", "protein", "domain", "struct", "combined"),
  model_type = "logistic_regression",
  cv_folds = 5
)

# Evaluate performance
performance <- evaluate_models(models)
print(performance)

# Extract feature importance
importance <- get_feature_importance(
  models,
  n_features = 50,
  scale = "gene"
)

# Visualize top features
plot_feature_importance(importance)

# Compare scales
compare_scales(models, metric = "bal_acc")

# Export for dashboard
export_results(
  models,
  output_dir = "model_outputs"
)
```

## Model interpretability

The package prioritizes interpretability through logistic regression:

### Coefficient interpretation

```r
# Get model coefficients
coefficients <- extract_coefficients(models$gene_model)

# Positive coefficients indicate features associated with resistance
# Negative coefficients indicate features associated with susceptibility

# Example output:
#   feature              coefficient   p_value
#   gyrA_mutation        2.34          <0.001
#   efflux_pump_ABC      1.87          <0.001
#   porin_loss          -0.45          0.023
```

### Feature ranking

```r
# Rank features by absolute coefficient magnitude
ranked_features <- rank_features(
  models,
  scale = "gene",
  n = 20
)

# Identify consistent features across drugs
cross_drug_features <- find_consistent_features(
  all_models,
  drugs = c("ciprofloxacin", "tetracycline"),
  min_rank = 10
)
```

## Advanced usage

### Custom model specifications

```r
# Specify custom logistic regression parameters
custom_spec <- logistic_reg(
  penalty = 0.01,
  mixture = 1  # LASSO regularization
) %>%
  set_engine("glmnet")

models <- train_amr_models(
  ml_data = ml_data,
  model_spec = custom_spec
)
```

### Cross-model analysis

```r
# Train models on different stratifications
country_models <- train_stratified_models(
  features = features,
  metadata = metadata,
  drug = "ciprofloxacin",
  stratify_by = "country",
  min_samples = 100
)

year_models <- train_stratified_models(
  features = features,
  metadata = metadata,
  drug = "ciprofloxacin",
  stratify_by = "collection_year",
  min_samples = 50
)

# Compare temporal stability
compare_temporal_models(year_models)
```

### Multi-drug prediction

```r
# Train models for drug classes
drug_classes <- list(
  fluoroquinolones = c("ciprofloxacin", "levofloxacin"),
  tetracyclines = c("tetracycline", "doxycycline"),
  aminoglycosides = c("gentamicin", "amikacin")
)

class_models <- train_drug_class_models(
  features = features,
  metadata = metadata,
  drug_classes = drug_classes,
  parallel = TRUE
)
```

## Performance benchmarks

Typical model performance varies by species and drug:

- **Balanced accuracy**: 0.75--0.95
- **F1 score**: 0.70--0.90
- **MCC**: 0.50--0.85

Training times depend on feature dimensions:
- Single drug, single scale: 1--5 minutes
- Single drug, all scales: 5--20 minutes
- Multiple drugs (parallel): 10--60 minutes

## Integration with amR suite

amRml integrates seamlessly with other amR packages:

```r
library(amRdata)
library(amRml)
library(amRshiny)

# 1. Curate data
features <- extract_features(...)

# 2. Train models (this package)
models <- train_amr_models(
  features = features,
  drug = "ciprofloxacin"
)

# 3. Visualize in dashboard
launch_dashboard(models = models)
```

## Model outputs

The package generates structured outputs for downstream analysis:

- `performances.tsv`: Metrics per model (balanced accuracy, F1, MCC, etc.)
- `feature_importance.tsv`: Ranked features per model
- `predictions.tsv`: Per-isolate predictions and probabilities
- `confusion_matrices.rds`: Detailed classification results
- `model_objects.rds`: Serialized model objects for reuse

These outputs are formatted for direct use in amRshiny or custom analyses.
